depth-bio-biochem-006.prompt: A hepatic glucose 6-phosphatase defect prevents fasting free-glucose export. Why can intact glycogen phosphorylase not fully compensate?
depth-bio-biochem-006.learningObjective: Apply carbohydrate control and dietary-lipid handling: mechanism challenges: Glycogen breakdown still feeds glucose 6-phosphate into the same blocked final release step.

depth-bio-biochem-007.subject: biochemistry
depth-bio-biochem-007.prompt: A patient has adequate luminal bile salts but severely deficient colipase. Which step is most directly compromised?
depth-bio-biochem-007.learningObjective: Apply carbohydrate control and dietary-lipid handling: mechanism challenges: Anchoring pancreatic lipase at the lipid–water interface in the presence of bile salts.

depth-bio-biochem-008.subject: biochemistry
depth-bio-biochem-008.prompt: Intestinal lipid hydrolysis and uptake are normal, but microsomal triglyceride transfer protein is absent in enterocytes. Which immediate defect best matches that location?
depth-bio-biochem-008.learningObjective: Apply carbohydrate control and dietary-lipid handling: mechanism challenges: Failure to assemble/export normal apoB-containing chylomicrons into lymph.

depth-bio-biochem-009.subject: biochemistry
depth-bio-biochem-009.prompt: Which comparison distinguishes the principal route for absorbed long-chain lipid from short-/medium-chain fatty acids?
depth-bio-biochem-009.learningObjective: Apply carbohydrate control and dietary-lipid handling: mechanism challenges: Long-chain lipid is mainly reassembled into chylomicrons for lymphatic transport; shorter fatty acids can enter portal blood without chylomicrons.
